speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your symptoms in detail, specifically regarding the rash on your trunk and extremities, and confirm if you have experienced any joint pain or a characteristic rash on your palms or soles.

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The timeline of fever, rhinorrhea, headache, followed by a facial rash sparing the nose and a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities is highly suggestive of a specific viral exanthem. Did you notice any swelling of her hands or feet, or any joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum)

The classic progression of a high fever (even if low-grade initially) for a few days followed by a sudden rash appearing after the fever starts or subsiding is the hallmark of this condition. Since the fever has likely resolved by the time the rash appeared, can you confirm if she is currently afebrile? I also need to verify her exact age to ensure this fits the typical age range for this virus.
